title: Strands span processor must ignore spans with no MLflow request ID
answers: strands autolog crashes with KeyError None on shared OpenTelemetry provider
strands autologging errors when another library's spans share the tracer provider
foreign span causes KeyError in Strands tracing
Strands agent tracing breaks when OTel spans from other instrumentation are present
body:
Symptom: With a shared OpenTelemetry provider, enabling Strands autologging raises an error when a span from other instrumentation (e.g. a remote-parent server span) is created in the same process.
Root cause: mlflow/strands/autolog.py:on_start calls tracer.span_processor.on_start, then reads SpanAttributeKey.REQUEST_ID. The base MLflow processor skips unknown child spans, so the attribute is None, and create_mlflow_span/register_span was still called with it, raising KeyError(None).
Fix pattern: After reading the request ID in on_start, return early when it is None, before create_mlflow_span and InMemoryTraceManager.register_span. Keep the early return inside the try/finally so the existing cleanup still runs.
Constraints: Applies only to the Strands processor's on_start. Any new span-processing path in this area that registers spans must perform the same None check, or foreign spans will crash it.
applies: mlflow/strands/autolog.py span processor used when MLflow shares a global OpenTelemetry tracer provider.
says: Strands autologging crashes when other tracing libraries share the same process.
Enabling agent tracing causes errors whenever foreign instrumentation spans are created.

Ignore unrelated external spans instead of crashing during Strands agent monitoring.

search: In mlflow/strands/autolog.py:on_start, the span processor must return early when SpanAttributeKey.REQUEST_ID is None before calling create_mlflow_span or InMemoryTraceManager.register_span. When sharing an OpenTelemetry tracer provider, foreign spans lack the request ID attribute and cause KeyError(None) if not skipped. The early return must remain inside try/finally to preserve cleanup, and any future span-processing path that registers spans must include the same None check.
